title: Privacy retention catalog and credentialed telemetry proxy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current observability pipelines (traces, logs, metrics) have fragmented retention and redaction controls. On-call and SRE teams cannot reliably discover which streams contain PII, nor can security teams audit ad-hoc access. We need a central policy catalog plus a lightweight enforcement proxy that 1) applies tenant-scoped retention and redaction rules at ingest and on replay, 2) enforces role-scoped reveal (credentialed unmasking) with an immutable access ledger, and 3) exposes a searchable catalog in Console for owners to declare retention/reveal policies. This ticket covers the engineering design and an MVP implementation for traces + trace snapshot replay.
acceptance_criteria: A searchable retention catalog exists in the backend: mappings for source -> retention TTL -> redaction profile -> owner
A credentialed telemetry proxy service can intercept replay/read requests and enforce RBAC policies before returning masked or full payloads
All reveal attempts are logged to an immutable access ledger with requestor identity, rationale, TTL of reveal, and link to PR/incident when applicable
Integrations: trace replay UI in Console calls proxy endpoint, and UI surfaces whether data returned was masked or unmasked
Migration: existing trace streams have default policies applied and a migration job runs to tag historic batches with catalog policy id
Automated tests for redaction profiles, policy evaluation, and access ledger insertion exist in CI with < 2 flakiness
Performance: proxy adds < 8ms p95 latency for metadata-only checks and < 20ms p95 for policy evaluation under nominal load (1000 rps test harness)
Security review sign-off in PR and threat-model notes committed
tasks: Design retention-catalog schema and durable store (proposal: single catalog table keyed by stream_id + environment)
Implement policy-evaluation engine (RBAC + attribute-based rules + reveal TTL)
Build credentialed telemetry proxy with: authentication hooks, policy fetch/cache, redaction application, access-ledger write
Add Console endpoints to read catalog entries and to request reveal operations via proxy
Create migration job to backfill catalog_id on existing trace bundles and tag in search index
Write end-to-end tests and load test scenario for proxy latency and throughput
Prepare rollout plan and feature flag gating per org tenant
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy catalog + proxy in staging and enable for internal Redwood tenant only
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable for 3 low-risk customers and SRE internal teams; collect latency and reveal audit logs for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (gradual): Gate by org setting in Console; default to tenant-configured policies, with opt-out for legacy streams
Phase 4 (enforce): After 30 days of pilot and policy adjustments, enable enforcement mode where proxy rejects unauthenticated reveal attempts
Fallback: Console UI to request temporary reveal with approver email that creates an entry in the access ledger and issues ephemeral reveal token
notes: Tradeoffs: enforcing redaction at ingest reduces risk but increases write path complexity; for MVP we'll enforce on replay and run a background scrubber for older buckets
Design decision: catalog will be authoritative for policy, but proxy will maintain an in-process LRU cache with TTL 30s to keep p95 low
KMS: reveal flows will use envelope encryption with short-lived unwrap tokens; work with security to define token lifetime
Data residency: catalog entries will include region affinity; proxy will consult region routing to avoid cross-region reveals when customer restricts data movement
Edge case: synthetic sampling for traces that contain PII markers should be dropped from public debugging exports by default
